epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per order with the order number, date and total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded, and the file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet.

features.description: Single capability: a customer exports their paid orders as a CSV file from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer with paid orders on the account page, When the customer triggers the export, Then a CSV file is downloaded to the customer's device.
Given a logged-in customer, When the customer triggers the export, Then the file contains only that customer's paid orders.
Given a customer who is not logged in, When the account page export is requested, Then the export is not provided.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story does not define which information the CSV file must contain (columns and fields), so a developer cannot know what the downloaded file should hold. Question for the PO: Which columns must the CSV export contain for each order?
stories.description: A customer can trigger an export of their paid orders from their account page and receive a CSV file. The export is limited to the orders of the logged-in customer. The control label and its placement on the page are left to the developer.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases
stories.title: Download paid orders as CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with one paid order and one cancelled order, When the customer exports orders, Then the file contains the paid order and does not contain the cancelled order.
Given a customer whose orders are all cancelled, When the customer exports orders, Then the file contains no order rows.
stories.aiReadyReason: The rule is clear: cancelled orders are excluded and only paid orders are exported, with two verifiable criteria covering the paid, cancelled and all-cancelled cases.
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from account page
stories.description: Orders that have been cancelled are not included in the exported file. Only paid orders are exported.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the file only lists orders that count as purchases

tasks.description: Update the backend order export query so that it selects only paid orders for the requesting customer and excludes cancelled orders. Expected result: the generated export contains paid orders only and no cancelled order rows.
tasks.title: Filter cancelled orders out of the export query

tasks.description: Write automated tests covering a customer with one paid and one cancelled order (file contains only the paid order) and a customer whose orders are all cancelled (file contains no order rows). Expected result: both scenarios pass.
tasks.title: Test export contents against acceptance criteria

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from the export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with three paid orders, When the customer exports orders, Then the file contains exactly three rows, one per order.
Given an exported row, When it is read, Then it contains the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT of that order.
stories.aiReadyReason: The delimiter and encoding of the file are explicitly undecided, so the file format cannot be implemented as specified. Question for the PO: Which delimiter and which character encoding must the CSV file use?
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from account page
Exclude cancelled orders from the export
stories.description: The export contains one row per paid order. Each row holds the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. The delimiter and the encoding of the file are not decided yet, so the file format cannot be finalised.
stories.iWant: each paid order to appear as one row with its order number, date and VAT-inclusive total
stories.soThat: I can review my order history in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export order number, date and VAT-inclusive total per row

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer exporting orders on a given date, When the file is downloaded, Then its name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with the date of the export.
Given a customer exporting orders, When the file is downloaded, Then the file name ends with the .csv extension.
stories.aiReadyReason: The file naming rule is explicit (orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv using the export date) and both criteria are verifiable by inspecting the downloaded file name.
dependencies: Download paid orders as CSV from account page
stories.description: The exported file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where YYYY-MM-DD is the date of the export.
stories.iWant: the exported file to carry a name that includes the export date
stories.soThat: I can recognise and organise my exports easily

tasks.description: Update the backend export response so the downloaded file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, using the date of the export, and ends with the .csv extension. Expected result: every export download carries this file name.
tasks.title: Generate export file name from export date

tasks.description: Write automated tests that export orders on a given date and verify the downloaded file name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with that date and the .csv extension. Expected result: both scenarios pass.
tasks.title: Test export file name against acceptance criteria

stories.title: Name the export file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
